mainTopic: רבי יוסי's exemption for one who errs while busy with a מצוה, then handling the לולב on שבת and the stages of a child's חינוך
overview: The amud opens with רבי יוסי's ruling from the משנה: someone who forgot it was שבת and carried his לולב into the public domain is exempt, because he was busy with a מצוה. The גמרא limits this to a case where he had not yet fulfilled the מצוה. It explains how that can happen: אביי says he held the לולב upside down, and רבא says he carried it in a כלי, which is a degrading way of holding it and does not count as taking. Next, רב הונא reports that רבי יוסי also exempts a כהן who ate an עולת העוף thinking it was a חטאת העוף. This teaches that the exemption applies even when no מצוה was actually done. A ברייתא seems to show רבי יוסי holding liable someone who slaughtered an uninspected תמיד on שבת. The answer is that this was a careless mistake, since he took the animal from the chamber of uninspected animals. A new משנה then teaches that a woman may take the לולב and return it to water on שבת, and that a קטן who knows how to shake it is obligated. The גמרא explains why the woman's case needed to be said. It then brings a ברייתא listing the stages at which a child begins each מצוה and status: לולב, ציצית, תפילין, learning תורה and קריאת שמע, טהרה, ספק טומאה, and receiving תרומה.

steps.title: The exemption applies only before he fulfilled the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רבי יוסי's exemption to a case where the person had not yet fulfilled the מצוה of לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only taught this (that he is exempt) when he had not yet fulfilled his obligation with it. But if he had already fulfilled it, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts a limit on the exemption in the משנה. רבי יוסי exempted the person only if he had not yet done the מצוה with the לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption exists because the person was carrying the לולב in order to do a מצוה. Once he has already shaken it, carrying it further does nothing for the מצוה. So if he then carries it into the public domain, he is liable to bring a חטאת like anyone else who violates שבת by mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of… (a limiting formula)
He fulfilled his obligation with it
Liable (here, to bring a חטאת)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the boundary of טעה בדבר מצוה: the exemption only covers a mistake made while actively pursuing a מצוה.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא יָצָא בּוֹ,
phrases.english: They only taught this where he had not yet fulfilled his obligation with it,
phrases.notes: This is talking about רבי יוסי's exemption in the משנה.

phrases.english: but if he had fulfilled his obligation with it, he is liable.
phrases.notes: Liable to a חטאת for carrying on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא יָצָא בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage by limiting רבי יוסי's ruling from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exemption for carrying a לולב on שבת by mistake applies only if he had not yet fulfilled the מצוה. Once he has fulfilled it, he is liable.

steps.title: Lifting the לולב already fulfills the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the limit: once he picked up the לולב, he has already fulfilled the מצוה, so the case of 'not yet fulfilled' seems impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: But from the moment he lifted it, he already fulfilled his obligation with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 1. You fulfill the מצוה of לולב just by lifting it, so anyone carrying it has already done the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of נטילת לולב is done the moment you pick it up. If that is true, the 'not yet fulfilled' case from Step 1 could never happen, and רבי יוסי's exemption would never apply. The גמרא needs a case where someone carries the לולב without having fulfilled the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: From the moment he lifted it
He fulfilled his obligation with it

phrases.english: But from the moment he lifted it, he fulfilled his obligation with it!
phrases.notes: Lifting is the act of the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the possibility of the case described in Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of 'שלא יצא בו' in Step 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lifting the לולב is itself the fulfillment, so a person carrying a לולב has already fulfilled the מצוה. The exempt case seems impossible.

steps.title: אביי: he held it upside down
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that he held the לולב upside down, which does not fulfill the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a case where he turned it over.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from Step 2. The person picked up the לולב upside down, so lifting it did not fulfill the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You fulfill the מצוה only by holding the לולב the way it grows, with the bottom down. If he held it upside down, he lifted it without doing the מצוה. He is still on his way to do the מצוה, so the exemption applies.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, a leading אמורא
When he turned it over (held it upside down)

phrases.english: Abaye said: When he turned it over.
phrases.notes: Holding it upside down does not fulfill the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any lifting of the לולב fulfills the מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Lifting it upside down does not fulfill the מצוה, so he carried it without having fulfilled it.

steps.title: רבא: he carried it inside a vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer: even if he did not turn it over, the case is where he carried the לולב inside a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say he did not turn it over. What case are we dealing with here? Where he carried it out inside a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second answer to the question in Step 2. The person carried the לולב inside a container, so he never actually took it in his hand to do the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not need the upside-down case. Holding the לולב through a vessel is not considered 'taking' it, so the מצוה was not fulfilled. He was still carrying it in order to do the מצוה later.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא, a leading אמורא and frequent disputant of אביי
Even if you say
With what case are we dealing here?
In a vessel/container

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא שֶׁלֹּא הֲפָכוֹ,
phrases.english: Rava said: Even if you say he did not turn it over,
with what are we dealing here?
For example, where he carried it out in a vessel.
phrases.notes: So he never directly 'took' the לולב.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא שֶׁלֹּא הֲפָכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to Step 2, offered instead of אביי's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the upside-down case could explain how he carried it without fulfilling the מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Carrying it inside a vessel also means he did not fulfill the מצוה.

steps.title: רבא himself said taking through another object counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא from his own ruling that taking by means of another object counts as taking.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it רבא himself who said: Taking by means of something else is considered taking!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבא's answer seems to contradict a rule he stated elsewhere. רבא held that holding the לולב through another item still counts as taking it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If taking through another object counts, then lifting the לולב inside a vessel should also fulfill the מצוה. That would bring back the problem of Step 2: he already fulfilled the מצוה, so he should be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it… (introduces a contradiction)
Taking by means of another object
It is called (counts as) taking

phrases.english: But isn't it Rava who said:

phrases.aramaic: לְקִיחָה עַל יְדֵי דָּבָר אַחֵר — שְׁמָהּ לְקִיחָה!
phrases.english: Taking by means of another object is considered taking!
phrases.notes: Based on the פסוק 'ולקחתם לכם'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in Step 4 using his own ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's answer that carrying in a כלי means the מצוה was not fulfilled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's own rule says taking through another object counts. So taking it in a כלי should fulfill the מצוה, which contradicts his answer.

steps.title: Respectful holding counts, degrading holding does not
steps.stepSummary: רבא's rule applies only when the other object is used respectfully, like a wrapping. Putting the לולב in a container is degrading and does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only when it is done in a respectful way. But in a degrading way, it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. רבא's rule covers respectful ways of holding the לולב, but not putting it in a vessel like ordinary cargo.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wrapping the לולב in a cloth to honor or beautify it still counts as taking it. Tossing it into a container to carry it is a degrading way to hold it and does not count. So רבא's answer in Step 4 stands: he never fulfilled the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only (limiting formula)
A respectful manner
A degrading manner

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to carry a לולב without fulfilling the מצוה: holding it upside down (אביי) or carrying it in a כלי in a degrading way (רבא). In both, רבי יוסי's exemption applies because the person had not yet fulfilled the מצוה.

phrases.english: These words apply in a respectful manner,
phrases.notes: Such as wrapping the לולב in a cloth.

phrases.english: but in a degrading manner, no.
phrases.notes: Like carrying it in a vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any taking through another object counts as taking.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only respectful taking through another object counts. Degrading taking, like carrying in a vessel, does not.

steps.title: רב הונא: a priest who mistakenly ate a burnt-offering bird
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reports that רבי יוסי exempted a כהן who ate an עולת העוף thinking it was a חטאת העוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: רבי יוסי used to say that if a bird burnt-offering was found among the bird offerings, and the כהן thought it was a bird sin-offering and ate it, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי יוסי, reported by רב הונא. A כהן ate a bird that was really a burnt-offering because he thought it was a sin-offering, and he is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is burned completely on the מזבח and may not be eaten, so eating it is normally מעילה and requires a קרבן. A חטאת העוף, however, is eaten by the כהנים as a מצוה. Since the כהן thought he was doing that מצוה, רבי יוסי exempts him.

keyTerms.meaning: רב הונא, an early אמורא
A bird burnt-offering, entirely burned and not eaten
A bird sin-offering, eaten by the כהנים
Among the other birds (mixed in where bird offerings are prepared)
Exempt

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Huna said: Rabbi Yosei would say,
a bird burnt-offering that was found among the birds,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְסָבוּר חַטַּאת הָעוֹף הִיא וַאֲכָלָהּ — פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: and he thought it was a bird sin-offering and ate it, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: Exempt from the קרבן for מעילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second case from רבי יוסי about making a mistake while pursuing a מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who ate an עולת העוף thinking it was a חטאת העוף is exempt, because he erred while trying to do a מצוה.

steps.title: What does רב הונא add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב הונא's report adds, since the משנה already teaches that one who erred while doing a מצוה is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? That one who erred in a matter of a מצוה is exempt? That is the same as the earlier case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions why רב הונא's statement is needed. It seems to teach the same rule as רבי יוסי's לולב case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי already taught in the משנה that someone who makes a mistake while busy with a מצוה is exempt. If רב הונא only repeats that rule with a new example, his statement seems to add nothing. The גמרא is looking for the new point.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us?
He made a mistake while involved in a מצוה
That is the same as that (no new point)

phrases.english: What is he teaching us,
that one who erred in a matter of a מצוה is exempt?
That is the same as that!
phrases.notes: Same as רבי יוסי's ruling about the לולב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב הונא's statement in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's report of רבי יוסי's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The principle of טעה בדבר מצוה פטור is already known from the לולב case, so the statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Here he did not actually do any מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in the לולב case a מצוה was actually done, but in the bird case none was. We might have thought that means no exemption, so רב הונא teaches that he is still exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that only there, where he erred in a matter of a מצוה, is he exempt, because he actually did a מצוה. But here, where he erred in a matter of a מצוה and did not do a מצוה, say he is not exempt. So רב הונא teaches us that he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the new point in רב הונא's statement. The exemption applies even when the mistake meant no מצוה was done at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the לולב case, the person was carrying the לולב to do a real מצוה, which he would actually perform. In the bird case, the כהן ate an עולה, so no מצוה happened at all. רב הונא teaches that the exemption depends on his intent to do a מצוה, not on whether a מצוה was actually done.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces the mistaken assumption)
There (the לולב case)
He performed a מצוה
He teaches us (the new point)

steps.whatToRemember: טעה בדבר מצוה פטור applies even when no מצוה was actually done. What matters is that the person made his mistake while trying to do a מצוה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'הָתָם' (there) means the לולב case from the משנה, and 'הָכָא' (here) means רב הונא's bird case. Do not mix them up.
steps.whyThisMatters: This widens the exemption: it depends on the person's intent to do a מצוה, not on whether a מצוה actually happened.

phrases.english: Lest you say:

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם הוּא דְּטָעָה בִּדְבַר מִצְוָה פָּטוּר —
phrases.english: It is only there that one who erred in a matter of a מצוה is exempt,
phrases.notes: The לולב case.

phrases.english: because he performed a מצוה.
But here, where he erred in a matter of a מצוה
phrases.notes: The bird offering case.

phrases.english: and did not perform a מצוה, say he is not exempt,
phrases.notes: Eating an עולה is not a מצוה.

phrases.english: so he teaches us (that he is exempt).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 8 by identifying the new point in רב הונא's statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exemption applies only when a מצוה was actually performed, as in the לולב case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exemption applies even when no מצוה was performed, as long as he erred while trying to do a מצוה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One who errs while involved in a מצוה is exempt even if, in the end, no מצוה was actually done.

steps.title: A ברייתא Where רבי יוסי Seems to Hold the Mistaken Person Liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's report from a ברייתא. There, רבי יוסי makes someone who slaughtered an uninspected תמיד on שבת liable to bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: רבי יוסי says that if someone slaughters the daily offering on שבת, and it was not inspected properly, he is liable to bring a חטאת and must bring a different daily offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רב הונא's claim that רבי יוסי exempts someone who made a mistake while doing a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering the תמיד on שבת is allowed only because it is a מצוה. If the animal turns out to have a blemish, no real מצוה was done, so the slaughter was a forbidden act on שבת. Here רבי יוסי says he is liable, which seems to contradict רב הונא's report that רבי יוסי exempts a person who erred while busy with a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (usually from a ברייתא)
The daily communal offering
Inspected for blemishes
Liable to bring a sin-offering for an accidental sin

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi Yosei says:
One who slaughters the daily offering
that was not inspected properly
phrases.notes: It turned out to have a blemish, so it was unfit.

phrases.english: on Shabbat is liable to bring a sin-offering,
and he needs another daily offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's report about רבי יוסי (step 7), which step 9 had just shown teaches something new.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's report that רבי יוסי exempts one who erred while doing a מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, רבי יוסי holds liable a person who erred while doing a מצוה and no מצוה was done. That is the same kind of case as the bird offering, yet he is liable.

steps.title: That Case Involved Taking From the Chamber of Uninspected Animals
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the ברייתא is about a careless mistake. The animal was taken from a chamber of uninspected animals, so the error does not count as a מצוה-related mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Bring proof from anything except that source. It was said about that ברייתא, in a chain from רב שמואל בר חתאי through רב המנונא סבא, רב יצחק בר אשיאן, and רב הונא back to רב, that it is talking about a case where he brought the animal from a chamber of animals that were not inspected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ברייתא is a special case where the person acted carelessly, so it does not contradict רב הונא's report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals for the תמיד must be taken only from the chamber of already-inspected animals. Taking one from the uninspected chamber is plain negligence, not an honest mistake made while busy with the מצוה. So רבי יוסי can still exempt real מצוה-mistakes, like the כהן with the bird offering, while holding the careless person liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for that one (that source is no proof)
It was said about it (an explanation of the ברייתא)
A chamber in the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The exemption for one who erred while busy with a מצוה applies only to an honest mistake. A careless mistake, like taking from the uninspected chamber, is not exempt.

phrases.english: He said to him: Except for that one.
phrases.notes: You cannot bring a proof from that ברייתא.

phrases.english: For it was stated about it,
Rav Shmuel bar Chatai said
that Rav Hamnuna the Elder said
that Rav Yitzchak bar Ashian said
that Rav Huna said that Rav said:
For example, where he brought it from a chamber
of animals that are not inspected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by narrowing the case in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא speaks of negligence
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to show that רבי יוסי holds liable anyone who erred during a מצוה when no מצוה was done.
steps.terutzMaskana: The liability comes from carelessness, because he took from the uninspected chamber. A real מצוה-mistake is still exempt according to רבי יוסי.

steps.title: משנה: Returning the לולב to Water on שבת, יום טוב, and חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a woman may take the לולב from her son or husband and put it back in water on שבת. רבי יהודה adds a scale: on שבת you may only put it back, on יום טוב you may add water, and on חול המועד you may change the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman may take the לולב from her son or her husband and put it back into water on שבת. רבי יהודה says: on שבת we put it back, on יום טוב we add water, and on חול המועד we change the water.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: how the לולב may be handled and kept fresh on שבת and other holy days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though a woman is not obligated in לולב, she may still handle it on שבת and return it to its water. רבי יהודה sets three levels of what is permitted: on שבת only returning it, on יום טוב also adding fresh water, and on חול המועד even replacing the water entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (start of a new משנה)
We return it (to the water)
We add (more water)
We change (the water)
חול המועד, the intermediate days of the festival

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A woman may receive (the lulav)
from the hand of her son or from the hand of her husband,
and return it to water on Shabbat.
Rabbi Yehuda says: On Shabbat we return it,
on Yom Tov we add (water),
and on Chol Hamoed we change (the water).

steps.triggerLanguage: מְקַבֶּלֶת אִשָּׁה מִיָּד בְּנָהּ וּמִיַּד בַּעְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic, after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may handle the לולב and return it to water on שבת. According to רבי יהודה, on יום טוב one may add water and on חול המועד one may change it.

steps.title: A Child Who Knows How to Shake Is Obligated in לולב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that a קטן who knows how to shake the לולב is obligated in the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A child who knows how to shake the לולב is obligated in לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a new rule: once a child knows how to shake the לולב properly, he must do the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטן is not obligated by the תורה. This obligation comes from the מצוה of חינוך, training children in מצוות. The point at which it begins is when the child knows how to do the shaking.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor (child under בר מצוה)
To shake / wave (the לולב)

steps.confusionAlert: חייב here does not mean a תורה obligation. A קטן is obligated only because of חינוך, the duty to train children in מצוות.

phrases.english: A minor who knows how to wave is obligated in lulav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a separate rule about who is obligated in לולב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטן who knows how to shake the לולב is obligated in לולב because of חינוך.

steps.title: Isn't the woman's permission obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed to say that a woman may take the לולב on שבת, since that seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה from step 12 and asks why it needed to say that a woman may take the לולב. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the son or husband may handle the לולב on שבת, it seems obvious that the woman may too. The question is why the משנה bothered to spell it out.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
It is obvious! (a challenge asking why something needed to be said)

phrases.english: Gemara: It is obvious!
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה's ruling that a woman may take the לולב on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה from step 12 to explain its wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to say that a woman may take the לולב on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Handling the לולב is clearly allowed, so stating it about a woman seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The woman's lack of obligation could have made it forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Since a woman is not obligated in לולב, we might have thought it is like מוקצה for her. The משנה teaches that she may still take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since a woman is not obligated in this מצוה, she should not take the לולב. So the משנה teaches us that she may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the חידוש. Without the משנה, we might have said a woman may not touch the לולב on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לולב is a time-bound positive מצוה, so a woman is not obligated in it. We might have thought the לולב has no use for her and is therefore like מוקצה. The משנה teaches that she may still take it and put it back in the water.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces the mistaken assumption)
Someone who is obligated (in this מצוה)
So it teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether a woman may do the מצוה of לולב. It is only whether she may move the לולב on שבת.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְאִשָּׁה לָאו בַּת חִיּוּבָא הִיא,
phrases.english: Since a woman is not obligated (in לולב),
phrases.notes: Because it's a positive מצוה that depends on a set time.

phrases.english: say that she should not take it,
phrases.notes: For her it would be like מוקצה.

phrases.english: so it teaches us (that she may).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows the חידוש by naming a mistaken assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a woman is not obligated, the לולב is like מוקצה for her and she may not take it.
steps.terutzMaskana: A woman may take the לולב and return it to the water on שבת.

steps.title: When a child begins different מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. A child who can shake a לולב is obligated in לולב. One who can wrap himself is obligated in ציצית. One who can guard תפילין gets תפילין from his father. One who can speak is taught תורה and קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A child who knows how to shake.' The Rabbis taught: a child who knows how to shake the לולב is obligated in לולב. One who knows how to wrap himself is obligated in ציצית. One who knows how to guard תפילין, his father buys him תפילין. One who knows how to speak, his father teaches him תורה and קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה from step 13. It then brings a ברייתא that expands it into a list of stages in a child's growth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each מצוה starts when the child is able to do it properly. Shaking means לולב, wrapping means ציצית, keeping clean means תפילין, and speaking means learning. This is the rabbinic obligation of חינוך, training a child in מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child under בר מצוה
To shake (the לולב)
The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
To wrap oneself in a garment
To guard תפילין, keeping his body clean while wearing them

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for the age of חינוך for each מצוה. The age depends on what the child can actually do.

phrases.english: 'A minor who knows how to shake.'
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A minor who knows how to shake is obligated in lulav;
(who knows how) to wrap himself is obligated in tzitzit;

phrases.aramaic: לִשְׁמוֹר תְּפִילִּין — אָבִיו לוֹקֵחַ לוֹ תְּפִילִּין,
phrases.english: (who knows how) to guard tefillin, his father buys him tefillin;
(who) knows how to speak, his father teaches him
Torah and the Shema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה and supports it with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child's obligation in each מצוה begins when he is able to do it properly.

steps.title: Which תורה does the father teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'תורה' means for a child who has just learned to speak.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'Torah' (taught to him)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition. A small child cannot learn all of תורה, so what exactly does the father teach him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the father teaches 'תורה' as soon as the child speaks. This clearly means a specific short text, and the גמרא wants to know which one.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asks for a definition)

phrases.english: What is the 'Torah'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תורה text a father teaches a child who has just begun to speak

steps.title: The verse 'תורה צוה לנו משה'
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא says it means the verse 'תורה צוה לנו משה מורשה קהלת יעקב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: the verse 'משה commanded us the Torah, an inheritance of the congregation of יעקב.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא answers. The 'תורה' a father first teaches is one well-known verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This verse sums up the bond between the Jewish people and the תורה: it is our inheritance. That makes it a fitting first verse for a small child.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who explains the ברייתא
Inheritance
The congregation of יעקב, the Jewish people

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said:
'Moses commanded us Torah,
an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob.'
phrases.notes: דברים 33:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse 'תורה צוה לנו משה מורשה קהלת יעקב'

steps.title: How much קריאת שמע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much of קריאת שמע the father teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'שמע' (taught to him)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second definition question, this time about how much of קריאת שמע is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קריאת שמע has several paragraphs, which is too much for a small child. The גמרא wants to know the minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: The recitation of 'שמע ישראל'

phrases.english: What is the 'Shema'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel definition question to step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much of קריאת שמע is taught to a young child

steps.title: Only the first verse
steps.stepSummary: The answer is the first verse of קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the father teaches only the first verse, 'שמע ישראל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first verse is the heart of קריאת שמע, accepting ה׳ as our King, so a small child starts there.

keyTerms.meaning: The first verse

steps.whatToRemember: A child who can speak is taught 'תורה צוה לנו משה' and the first verse of שמע.

phrases.english: The first verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.

steps.title: A child who guards his body or hands from טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. If a child knows how to keep his body, or his hands, from טומאה, pure food that he touched may still be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who knows how to guard his body: we may eat pure foods that touched his body. One who knows how to guard his hands: we may eat pure foods that touched his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the same ברייתא from step 16, which now lists stages in the area of טהרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child who does not understand טומאה is assumed to have touched impure things. Once he knows how to protect himself, he is trusted, and food he touched stays pure. Body and hands are separate stages, because hands touch things without our noticing.

keyTerms.meaning: Food kept in a state of ritual purity
His body
His hands

phrases.english: One who knows how to guard his body —
we may eat pure foods (that touched) his body.
(One who knows how) to guard his hands —
we may eat pure foods (that touched) his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the ברייתא again after the definitions of steps 17–20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child who can guard his body or his hands from טומאה is trusted, so pure food he touched stays pure.

steps.title: A child who can be asked about a doubt of טומאה
steps.stepSummary: A child who can answer questions is treated like an adult in cases of doubtful טומאה. A doubt in a private domain is impure, and a doubt in a public domain is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who knows how to be asked: in a private domain, his doubt is impure; in a public domain, his doubt is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives another stage. Once a child can answer questions clearly, the normal rules of ספק טומאה apply to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an adult, the rule of ספק טומאה is that a doubt in a רשות היחיד is impure and a doubt in a רשות הרבים is pure. A child who cannot be questioned does not fall under this rule, so his doubts are ruled pure even in a private domain. Once he can be asked, the adult rule applies to him.

keyTerms.meaning: To be asked, able to answer questions clearly
A private domain
A public domain
His case of doubt

steps.confusionAlert: 'Impure' and 'pure' here are not about the child as a person. They describe how we rule on an item when it is unclear whether טומאה touched it.

phrases.english: One who knows how to be asked,
in a private domain, his doubt is impure;
in a public domain, his doubt is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of טהרה stages in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child who can be questioned follows the adult rules of ספק טומאה: impure in a private domain, pure in a public domain.

steps.title: A child כהן who can bless the people receives תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A child כהן who knows how to say ברכת כהנים is given תרומה at the threshing floors, like any other כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who knows how to spread his hands (for the Priestly Blessing): we give him a share of תרומה at the threshing floors.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a stage for a child כהן. Once he can do ברכת כהנים, he receives תרומה publicly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Handing out תרומה at the public threshing floor openly shows that someone is a recognized כהן. A child who can already say ברכת כהנים is treated as a כהן there, just like an adult.

keyTerms.meaning: To spread his hands, saying ברכת כהנים
The portion of produce given to a כהן
The threshing floors, where produce is processed and תרומה is given out

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא ties each stage of a child's ability to a matching halachic status: לולב, ציצית, תפילין, learning, טהרה, ספק טומאה, and receiving תרומה.

phrases.english: One who knows how to spread his hands —
we distribute terumah to him at the threshing floors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last item in the ברייתא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child כהן who can say ברכת כהנים is given תרומה at the threshing floors.
